systems.name: Pulsar FOC, polar planes (Xona Space Systems)
systems.orbit_source: J. Leclère, T. Marathe, T. G. R. Reid (Xona Space Systems), Insights into Xona Pulsar LEO PNT: Constellation, Signals, and Receiver Design, ION GNSS+ 2025, arXiv:2509.19551, section 2.2 and Table 1 (orbit radius 7451.0 km, so an Earth radius of 6371 km)

claims.source: arXiv:2509.19551, Table 1: orbital period 106.7 min
arXiv:2509.19551, Table 1: satellite orbital speed 7314.1 m/s
arXiv:2509.19551, Table 1: maximum relative speed to a static user 6327.4 m/s (polar orbit)
arXiv:2509.19551, Table 1: max. L1 band carrier Doppler 33628.5 Hz; Table 2: X1 carrier 1593.3225 MHz
arXiv:2509.19551, Table 1: max. L5 band carrier Doppler 25126.9 Hz; Table 2: X5 carrier 1190.51625 MHz
arXiv:2509.19551, section 2.2: 'the footprint radius is about 3864 km for a Pulsar FOC satellite ... (with a 0° elevation mask)'
claims.note: the paper calls this figure the footprint radius; it is the slant range to a satellite on the horizon, and the ground arc is reported beside it

claims.source: arXiv:2509.19551, section 2.2: Doppler 'is about 8 times greater for Pulsar than for GPS' (GPS orbit from Table 1: 20180 km, 55°)
claims.note: the stated figure is approximate ('about'), hence the 15 % tolerance

claims.source: arXiv:2509.19551, section 2.2: the Doppler rate 'is about 250 times higher for the Pulsar FOC constellation'
claims.note: the stated figure is approximate ('about'), hence the 20 % tolerance

claims.source: arXiv:2509.19551, section 6.2: 'The largest carrier Doppler rate is up to −230 Hz/s on X1 and −172 Hz/s on X5'
claims.note: the paper gives the magnitude for the FOC constellation; the polar planes give the larger rate

claims.source: arXiv:2509.19551, section 6.2: '... and −172 Hz/s on X5'
